0.label: hooded_figure_crossed_bands_over_serpent
0.description: The pasted drawing: a face inside a pointed triangular hood, two bands crossing in an X over the body with a ring at the crossing and a hand holding a small object, fringed wing-like panels to the sides, a small seated figure at the foot, and a wavy serpent with a head running along the base; posts topped with small heads at each side.
0.iconography: The pointed hood and crossed bands are the war leader's marks seen on the Ado-Ekiti door (#23, #34). The serpent along the ground line is the door's frame-serpent — the boundary animal. Captioned as a scene 'from mythology'.

panel.title: Mount sheet: a hooded figure with crossed bands above a serpent, from a Yoruba compound door (pl. 183)
panel.object_type: archive mount sheet with a partial drawing of a door (after Frobenius 1923, pl. 183)
panel.summary: A small partial drawing ('right figure') from Plate 183, captioned 'West African wood carving. Door of a Yoruba compound with scenes from mythology; figures in relief filling the surface. Collection of the D.I.A.F.E. 1910.'

register_readings.reading: One figure: pointed hood, crossed bands, a small figure at its feet, a serpent along the base.

panel.composition: A figure filling a door panel between two posts, standing on a serpent ground line.
panel.narrative: Frobenius called this door 'mythological', but the figure has the same pointed hood and crossed bands as the leaders on the Ado-Ekiti war door. That shows the problem with the 1910 labels: what the collector read as myth may be a portrait of a known war chief. The serpent on the ground line frames the scene as on the other doors.
panel.hypotheses: Supports 'war' if the crossed bands mark a war leader; the collector's 'mythology' label should not settle it.
cross_panel_links: Pointed hood and crossed bands: EBA-Div_00303 (#23, #34), KBA_17553 (#1), KBA_19155.
uncertainties: A partial drawing; the rest of the door is not shown.
The side panels could be a cloak, fans or shields.
